Prerequisite: A FortiSIEM license, EPS based (Devices and Total EPS) or GB per day (Raw Event GB Per Day), that covers the devices and the event rate in scope and matches the Supervisor (the UUID of a virtual appliance, the serial number of a hardware appliance)
What it enables: Devices that send logs or are monitored count against the device license (devices beyond it are tagged Unmanaged or not added to the CMDB), and events beyond the licensed EPS are dropped after the unused events are spent
How to put it in place: Apply the license from Fortinet at installation; GUI: Admin > License > General (check Devices, Total EPS or Raw Event GB Per Day, and the expiry dates); GUI: Admin > License > Usage
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Licensing" (Key Concepts), "Step 2 - Install License", "Viewing License Information", and "License Enforcement" (CMDB Device and EPS License Enforcement)

Prerequisite: A Host Collector license (the Host Collectors value of the license) for the Windows and Linux agents
What it enables: Windows and Linux Host Collectors (agents) register and send events; at the license limit a new Host Collector cannot register
How to put it in place: Buy the Host Collector count with the license; GUI: Admin > License > General (Host Collectors value and expiry)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Viewing License Information", "License Enforcement" (Host Collector License Enforcement), and "Adding Linux Collectors" (Linux Collectors require a license)

Prerequisite: The FortiGuard IOC Service in the license (FortiGuard Threat Intelligence is subscription based)
What it enables: The FortiGuard IOC feeds (malware IPs, domains, and URLs) and IOC lookups, and the FortiGate IPS signature to CVE mapping pulled from FortiGuard
How to put it in place: Buy the subscription; GUI: Admin > License > General (IOC Service value and expiry); then enable the IOC service on the FortiGuard folders in GUI: Resources > Malware IPs
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Licensing", "Viewing License Information" (IOC Service), "Working with FortiGuard Threat Feeds", and the IPS false positive detection notes (the FortiGuard IOC license must be enabled)

Prerequisite: On 7.5.0 and later, a FortiSIEM license key file obtained for 7.5.0 or later (not the Legacy License Key file), which includes its own certificate
What it enables: Authentication to FortiGuard for IOC download, Collector and agent image hash download, and content updates, and mutual authentication when a FortiSIEM node is added
How to put it in place: Download the new license key file from FortiCare after an upgrade from a release before 7.5.0; GUI: Admin > License > Upload License
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "What's New in 7.6.0", Known Issues / Implementation Notes, "Installation and Upgrade Related" (step 7: the license certificate and why it is needed)

Prerequisite: The Service Provider installation type
What it enables: Organizations (multi-tenancy) with logical separation of devices, users, and logs
How to put it in place: Choose the Service Provider installation type when FortiSIEM is first installed
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Multi-tenancy and Organizations" (Key Concepts)

Prerequisite: ClickHouse as the event database, with the Supervisor and Workers set up as ClickHouse Keeper, data, and query nodes
What it enables: The features that work only on ClickHouse: ClickHouse event integrity, scheduled and advanced search rules, field analytics and large result sets, ClickHouse archive and tiers, partition checks, and secure ClickHouse communication
How to put it in place: GUI: Admin > Setup > Storage (ClickHouse); GUI: Admin > Settings > Database > ClickHouse Config (Test, then Deploy)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Configuring Storage" (Configuring ClickHouse Storage on Supervisor Node and on Worker Node) and "ClickHouse Configuration"; the release notes entries named in the rows

Prerequisite: EventDB as the event database (on local disk or NFS)
What it enables: EventDB event log integrity (a checksum for each event file, Validate, Validate All, export)
How to put it in place: GUI: Admin > Setup > Storage (EventDB)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Configuring EventDB Based Deployment" and "Validating Event Log Integrity for EventDB"

Prerequisite: The external storage that the storage settings point to: an NFS server (EventDB on NFS, EventDB archive, ClickHouse warm and cold tiers), an Elasticsearch cluster, or an AWS S3 or Google Cloud Storage bucket (ClickHouse archive), separate from the Supervisor and Workers
What it enables: Online event storage on NFS or Elasticsearch, and archive storage outside the FortiSIEM nodes
How to put it in place: Set up the NFS server, Elasticsearch cluster, or bucket first, then select it in GUI: Admin > Setup > Storage
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Getting Started" (set up external storage if needed; Step 3 - Specify Event Database Storage), "Configuring ClickHouse Archive Storage", "Creating EventDB Archive Storage", "Creating Elasticsearch Online Storage", and "ClickHouse Archive to Google Cloud Storage (GCS)"

Prerequisite: FortiSIEM Collectors installed and defined on the Supervisor (name and Guaranteed EPS), with the Workers that receive their events set as Event Upload Workers
What it enables: Collector registration and the features that run on Collectors: event upload to the Workers, Collector health, Collector high availability (two or more Collectors on the same network as the VIP), event tagging on the Collectors, and the Host Collectors that send their logs to Collectors
How to put it in place: Install the Collector node; GUI: Admin > Setup > Collector (Name, Guaranteed EPS); GUI: Admin > Settings > System > Cluster Config (Event Upload Workers)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Setting Collectors (Enterprise)", "Setting Organizations and Collectors (Service Provider)", "Event Upload Worker Configuration", "Collector High Availability Configuration", and "Windows and Linux Host Collectors"; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Installing on RHEL 9.6 for FIPS 140-3 Crypto Module Support, "Register Collectors"

Prerequisite: Fully qualified domain names in DNS for the Supervisor, Workers, and Collectors, used as their host names, with the Supervisor FQDN set in FortiSIEM
What it enables: Certificates whose subject matches each node, Collector registration by the Supervisor FQDN, and SAML (the FQDN must match the domain in the identity provider's ACS URL)
How to put it in place: Create the DNS records and set each host name to its FQDN; GUI: Admin > Settings > System > FQDN
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Configuring CA Certificates, "Prerequisites"; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "FQDN" and "External Authentication Settings" (Configure FortiSIEM Users for SAML Authentication)

Prerequisite: Certificates issued by a DoD-approved certification authority for the Supervisor, Workers, and Collectors (per node with a subject that matches the node FQDN, or a wildcard certificate), with their private keys and CA chain
What it enables: CA-signed certificates for the GUI and the Collector HTTPS connections, peer verification, and certificate verification for the backend SSL sockets
How to put it in place: Request the certificates from the DoD PKI and copy them to /etc/httpd/conf.d on each node (see the certificate rows)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Configuring CA Certificates, "Prerequisites" and "Collector to Supervisor HTTPS Comm."; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Hardening Guide, "Enable Public CA Signed SSL Certificates"

Prerequisite: The devices, hosts, and cloud services in scope, set to send their logs to FortiSIEM (syslog, SNMP traps, NetFlow, or a Kafka topic) or given the accounts and API credentials that FortiSIEM uses to discover them and pull their events
What it enables: Event collection, discovery into the CMDB, Security Fabric and FortiClient EMS discovery, and event pulling from devices and services
How to put it in place: Configure each device to send its logs to a Collector or Worker, or create the account it needs; GUI: Admin > Setup > Credentials (associate the credential with the IP ranges or hosts and test it)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Setting Credentials", "Discovering Devices", "Editing Event Pulling", and "Kafka Settings" (Setting Up Consumer)

Prerequisite: The enclave aggregation server or second log server that receives forwarded events, listening for syslog over TCP over SSL with a certificate that FortiSIEM can validate
What it enables: Real-time off-loading of events to another system over an encrypted, reliable connection
How to put it in place: Set up the receiving server; where it verifies the FortiSIEM certificate, add tls_certificate_file=<CERT_FILE>; tls_key_file=<KEY_FILE> (in the phEventForwarder section of phoenix_config.txt on the forwarding nodes)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Forwarding Events to External Systems" and "Event Forwarding"; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Configuring CA Certificates, "Event Forwarding from FortiSIEM to an External System Using syslog/TLS"

Prerequisite: A backup destination on another system: an SFTP server or AWS S3 bucket for ClickHouse backups, and an external location with enough space for the CMDB, EventDB, and SVN copies (also for the backup and restore around disk encryption of an existing node)
What it enables: Backups of the CMDB, SVN, and event data kept off the FortiSIEM nodes, and disk encryption of a node that already holds data
How to put it in place: Prepare the SFTP server or S3 bucket and the backup share before scheduling the backups
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Backing Up and Restoring Databases" and "ClickHouse Backup and Restore Steps" (Step 1: Prepare the SFTP server; Backup to AWS S3); FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Disk Encryption for FortiSIEM Virtual Machine (backup location for an existing installation)

Prerequisite: An SMTP mail server (email gateway) that accepts TLS, and email addresses for the recipients
What it enables: Email for incident notification and scheduled reports
How to put it in place: GUI: Admin > Settings > System > Email (server, port, Secure Connection (TLS), and credentials)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Step 7 - Add Email Gateway", "Email Settings" (General Email Server Settings), and "Scheduled Report Settings"

Prerequisite: A webhook URL from the messaging service that receives incident notifications (Microsoft Teams, WhatsApp, Slack, Telegram, or a custom receiver)
What it enables: Incident notification by webhook
How to put it in place: Create the webhook in the messaging service, then add it in GUI: Admin > Settings > Analytics > Incident Notification
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Webhook for Incident Notification" and "Notifying Microsoft Teams Users via Webhook" (Step 1 - Get Microsoft Teams Webhook URL)

Prerequisite: An external ticketing system (ServiceNow, Jira, ConnectWise, or Salesforce) with an account for FortiSIEM, and its certificate trusted by FortiSIEM
What it enables: Cases and incidents sent to and synchronized with the ticketing system
How to put it in place: Create the integration account in the ticketing system; import its certificate with keytool -import -trustcacerts -alias <ALIAS> -keystore /opt/glassfish/domains/domain1/config/cacerts.jks -file <CERT_FILE>
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Ticketing System Integrations"; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Configuring CA Certificates, "Java-based HTTPS Comm. From FortiSIEM to External Websites"

Prerequisite: Access to the external threat intelligence sources in use (feed URLs or STIX/TAXII 2.1 servers, with their credentials), and their certificates trusted by FortiSIEM
What it enables: Download of external threat intelligence into the malware IP, domain, URL, and hash groups
How to put it in place: Get the feed URL and credentials from the provider; import its certificate with keytool -import -trustcacerts -alias <ALIAS> -keystore /opt/glassfish/domains/domain1/config/cacerts.jks -file <CERT_FILE>
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "External Threat Intelligence Integration" and "Generic STIX/TAXII 2.1 Integration for collecting External Threat Intelligence"; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Configuring CA Certificates, "Java-based HTTPS Comm. From FortiSIEM to External Websites"

Prerequisite: Outbound TCP 443 from the Supervisor to update.fortiguard.net, directly or through a proxy (offline FortiGuard IOC download is not supported for air-gapped deployments)
What it enables: The FortiGuard IOC feed and lookups, validation of Collector and Host Collector packages against the hash in FortiGuard, and content updates
How to put it in place: Allow the connection in the enclave firewall; where a proxy is required, GUI: Admin > Settings > System > FortiGuard Proxy
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Internet Connectivity Requirements" (Working with FortiGuard Threat Feeds), "FortiGuard Proxy", and "Image Server Settings"

Prerequisite: Outbound TCP 443 from each node to the FortiSIEM Rocky Linux repositories (os-pkgs-cdn, os-pkgs-r9, and before 7.5.0 os-pkgs-r8, at fortisiem.fortinet.com), or an offline repository server
What it enables: Operating system updates without a FortiSIEM upgrade, and installation of operating system packages such as cryptsetup
How to put it in place: Allow the connections in the enclave firewall, or set up an offline repository server
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 OS Update Lifecycle, "FortiSIEM OS Update Procedure" (Notes); FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Internet Connectivity Requirements"; FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Disk Encryption for FortiSIEM Virtual Machine, "Step 1a: Download and Install"

Prerequisite: An LDAP directory (Microsoft Active Directory) reachable over LDAPS or LDAPTLS, with a certificate whose CN or subject alternative name matches the server name in the profile (self-signed certificates fail the check), and directory groups for the roles
What it enables: External authentication of GUI users against the directory, with X.509 certificate checking, and AD group to role mapping
How to put it in place: Install the certificate on the directory server; GUI: Admin > Settings > General > External Authentication (Protocol LDAPS or LDAPTLS, Check Certificate)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "External Authentication Settings" (Case 1: LDAP/LDAPS/LDAPTLS Profile)

Prerequisite: A RADIUS server (for example FortiAuthenticator) with FortiSIEM defined as a RADIUS client with a shared secret
What it enables: RADIUS authentication of GUI users (7.4.0 and later)
How to put it in place: Add FortiSIEM as a RADIUS client on the server; GUI: Admin > Settings > General > External Authentication (Protocol RADIUS, Shared Secret; Test)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "Example 2: Configuring FortiSIEM Users for RADIUS/LDAP Authentication with FortiAuthenticator (FAC)" and "What's New in 7.4.0"

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider (for example Azure AD, Okta, or FortiAuthenticator) that enforces CAC, with FortiSIEM defined as a service provider and the users, organizations, and roles mapped
What it enables: SAML single sign-on, multifactor and CAC logon through the identity provider, and SAML role mapping
How to put it in place: Configure the identity provider and collect its endpoint and certificate; GUI: Admin > Settings > General > External Authentication (Protocol SAML, Issuer, Certificate)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "External Authentication Settings" (Configure FortiSIEM Users for SAML Authentication, Step 1 - Preparation)

Prerequisite: A Duo Security account with an application for FortiSIEM (API hostname, integration key, secret key, and application key) and the FortiSIEM users enrolled in Duo
What it enables: Duo two-factor authentication for GUI users
How to put it in place: Obtain the keys from Duo Security; GUI: Admin > Settings > General > External Authentication (Protocol Duo)
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 User Guide, "External Authentication Settings" (Case 3: Duo Profile for 2 Factor Authentication) and "Example 5: Configuring FortiSIEM Users for 2 Factor Authentication with Duo Security"

Prerequisite: Internal, DoD-approved NTP servers, set on the hypervisor host of each virtual node (for ESX, the host Time Configuration)
What it enables: Accurate time on every node for event receive time stamps and time synchronization
How to put it in place: Enter the NTP servers in the host's Configure > System > Time Configuration on ESX
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 ESX Installation Guide, "Set Network Time Protocol for ESX"

Prerequisite: FIPS mode on every FortiSIEM node that a FIPS node talks to, and devices that support FIPS-compliant algorithms
What it enables: FIPS mode without broken communication: a FIPS-compliant node communicates only with FIPS-compliant nodes, and communication with a device that does not support FIPS breaks
How to put it in place: configFSM.sh (FIPS option on each Supervisor, Worker, and Collector); replace or exclude devices that do not support FIPS
Source: FortiSIEM 7.6.0 Hardening Guide, "Ensure Strong Cryptographic Algorithms are Enabled"
